newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RAIN DELAYS HARVESTING BY AT LEAST A WEEK.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RAIN DELAYS HARVESTING BY AT LEAST A WEEK.

text.p: Rains in Hungary have delayed harvesting by at least one week and current estimates said it could be finished around August 20, officials said on Monday.
"It is safe to say that harvesting has been delayed by at least one week," Zsolt Kiraly of the Agriculture Ministry told Reuters.
He added that wheat, oat and rye harvesting was likely to be finished around August 20 at the earliest.
Attila Bussay of the National Meteorological Service (OMSZ) said that over the last five days only north Hungarian counties saw significant rains of 55-60 millimeters.
He added that even little or moderate rain can cause delays in harvesting and was also likely to deteriorate the quality of the wheat crop.
But he also said that current weather conditions were favourable for maize.
"Weather that is bad for wheat harvesting is usually good for maize," he said, adding, however, that the rainy weather was somewhat colder than the ideal temperature for maize.
"Maize likes hot and humid weather. In Hungary, you either have hot and dry or cold and humid weather".
Market participants expected this year's maize crop to slightly exceed last year's already good six million tonnes.

The latest trade estimates put this year's wheat crop to between four and 4.5 million tonnes, compared with 3.9 million in 1996 and eariler ministry estimates of five million tonnes, but with a relatively high percentage of low-quality wheat.
Traders said earlier that this year the customary 60-40 milling wheat-to-feed wheat ratio was more likely to be 40-60.
However, ministry officials said it was too early to have even a rough estimate of wheat quality.
"Less than one third of the wheat has been harvested and most producers start harvesting on their best lots," Kiraly said.
Balazs Tarjan head of the ministry's agricultural regime office added that with producers and traders having different interests, there was a lot of lobbying designed to move grains prices.
"Most of what we hear at the moment is driven by different interests," he said, but added that although traders would be interested to see lower prices, wheat futures prices were rising.
Current weather forecasts expected scattered rainshowers over the northern half of Hungary and moderate to heavy rains throughout the country by Friday.
